subject: mixed versus heavy penalties for epistasis

messages.author: e728ca3dc3a1a072
messages.subject: mixed versus heavy penalties for epistasis
parts:
Hi Karl,

I was wondering if you could suggest some literature for an explanation/justification of using the mixed (versus just the heavy) penalties for epistasis in the stepwise procedure?

I'm analyzing some results as the mean trait value over many years, and I'm finding that the stepwise model I get using mixed penalties for epistasis is more representative of the QTL results from all individual years (and had a higher overall LOD score) for our particular mapping population. I would like to have some additional literature to back up the choice of using mixed penalties if possible.

Thanks,

Chris

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] mixed versus heavy penalties for epistasis
parts:
Just the original paper, I think.

> Manichaikul A, Moon JY, Sen Ś, Yandell BS, Broman KW (2009) A model selection approach for the identification of quantitative trait loci in experimental crosses, allowing epistasis. Genetics 181:1077-1086 https://doi.org/10.1534/genetics.108.094565

Maybe also Chapter 9 of the R/qtl book (https://rqtl.org/book), but I don't think much different from what's in the 2009 paper.

karl
